summary.title: A Visual Git Reference
summary.one_liner: A visual guide to how common git commands (add, commit, reset, checkout, merge, rebase, cherry-pick) move content between the working directory, stage, and commit history.
keywords: how to discard local changes git
takeaways: The stage (index), working directory, and HEAD commit history are three places git copies files between, and git add, commit, reset, and checkout each move them differently.
git reset -- files unstages changes, git checkout -- files discards working-directory edits, and git checkout HEAD -- files resets both stage and working directory.
Committing with a detached HEAD creates commits that no branch references, so they can be lost unless you create a named branch.
A merge creates a commit with two parents (three-way merge by default), while a rebase replays commits onto another branch for a linear history.
Git stores file contents as blobs and directories as trees in the object database, with the index mapping filenames to blob IDs.
summary.summary: The page is a visual reference for common git commands, using diagrams of commits, branches, and HEAD to show what each command does. It explains the relationship between the working directory, the stage (index), and commit history, then covers commit, checkout, detached HEAD, reset, merge, cherry-pick, and rebase. A technical notes section describes how git stores blobs, trees, and commits, and a final walkthrough runs shell commands in a test repository to show file states changing after each command.
